The source document is registered in `sources/index.yaml` as `gr-202307061137387522` (date 2023-07-05).

Do this:
1. Read CLAUDE.md (the rulebook rules), the change set, and the files of the affected scheme(s): mh.sanjay_gandhi_niradhar.
2. Apply every change in the change set, following CLAUDE.md exactly:
   - parameter change: add a new dated value under `values:` starting 2023-07-05. Never edit or delete older values.
   - condition change: set `valid_until` on the old condition to the day before 2023-07-05, and add a new condition with the same id and `valid_from: 2023-07-05`.
   - condition removed: only set `valid_until` to the day before 2023-07-05.
   - every new value or condition gets `source` / `metadata.reference` with doc `gr-202307061137387522`, page, clause, quote (copied from the change set) and quote_en.
   - if a change needs a new person field, add it to `schema/person.yaml` with a default that keeps existing results unchanged and never grants extra eligibility or money (a fact that unlocks a higher limit or amount, such as being disabled, defaults to false).
3. Add test citizens to `tests/` for every change, dated on or after 2023-07-05: just below, at, and just above each limit, plus one case dated before 2023-07-05 proving the old rule still applies. Each case cites `GR 202307061137387522 p.<page> clause <clause>` in `source`.
4. Add an entry at the top of CHANGELOG.md (English, Hindi, Marathi) linking to the document.
5. Run `python -m niyam_rulebook test` and fix problems until it prints `0 failed` with no PROBLEM lines.
6. Do not run git. Do not edit files outside schemes/, parameters/, tests/, sources/, glossary/, schema/ and CHANGELOG.md.

Finish with a short summary of what you changed and the final test result.

1	# Changelog
2	
3	Plain-language record of every rule change. Newest first. Each entry is in
4	English, Hindi and Marathi and links to its source.
5	
6	## 1 September 2019: Sanjay Gandhi Niradhar Anudan Yojana (GR dated 20 August 2019)
7	
8	- English: The scheme starts on 1 September 2019 with revised rules. People who have lived in Maharashtra for at least 15 years, are aged 18 to 64, have a family income up to Rs 21,000 a year (Rs 50,000 for disabled people), and get no regular benefit from another government scheme, get Rs 1,000 a month. Widows with one child get Rs 1,100 and widows with two or more children get Rs 1,200.
9	- हिंदी: संजय गांधी निराधार अनुदान योजना 1 सितंबर 2019 से संशोधित नियमों के साथ शुरू होती है। जो व्यक्ति महाराष्ट्र में कम से कम 15 वर्ष से रह रहे हैं, 18 से 64 वर्ष की आयु के हैं, जिनके परिवार की वार्षिक आय 21,000 रुपये तक है (दिव्यांगों के लिए 50,000 रुपये), और किसी अन्य सरकारी योजना से नियमित मासिक लाभ नहीं लेते, उन्हें हर महीने 1,000 रुपये मिलेंगे। एक अपत्य वाली विधवाओं को 1,100 रुपये और दो या अधिक अपत्य वाली विधवाओं को 1,200 रुपये मिलेंगे।

1	# Interpretation glossary: Maharashtra government resolutions
2	
3	How Niyam reads recurring legal phrases. The agent reads this file before
4	extracting or resolving, and adds an entry whenever it settles an ambiguity.
5	Each entry cites where the interpretation came from. Entries marked
6	"needs human confirmation" have not been confirmed by a person yet.
7	
8	## "पेक्षा जास्त नसावे" (should not be more than)
9	Inclusive upper limit: a value equal to the limit is allowed.
10	Source: GR 202406281814018230, clause 4(5), income "not more than Rs 2.50 lakh".
11	
12	## "पेक्षा जास्त" (more than)
13	Strict comparison: a value equal to the limit is not "more than" the limit.
14	Source: GR 202406281814018230, clauses 5(4) and 5(7).
15	
16	## "किंवा त्यापेक्षा जास्त" (or more than that)
17	Inclusive: a value equal to the limit counts.
18	
19	## "वयाची N वर्षे पूर्ण होईपर्यंत" (until N years of age are completed)
20	Niyam stores ages as completed years and treats the upper age N as eligible
21	(age N is inside the range). This matches the scheme summary in the same GR,
22	"21 ते 60 या वर्ष वयोगटातील" (in the 21 to 60 age group).
23	Status: needs human confirmation. A strict reading could end eligibility on the
24	Nth birthday.
25	
26	## "कुटुंब" (family)
27	Not yet defined in the rulebook. Niyam treats family facts (income, tax payer,
28	government job, land, vehicle) as reported by the applicant for her household.
29	
30	## Dates
31	A GR applies from its own date unless it states another start date.
32	A change to an earlier GR keeps the earlier value in history (a new dated value
33	is added; old values are never edited).

35	## "रुपये N पर्यंत" (up to Rs N)
36	Inclusive upper limit: a value equal to N qualifies, and a value above N does not (for example Rs 21,001 against a Rs 21,000 limit).

The rulebook now reflects the 5 July 2023 GR: the monthly amount rises from Rs 1,000 to Rs 1,500 for all beneficiaries, and the widow tiers (1 child, 2+ children) also go to Rs 1,500. `python -m niyam_rulebook test` ends with `tests: 60 passed, 0 failed` and no PROBLEM lines.

**What changed**
- **Parameters:** I added a `2023-07-05` value of 1500 to `monthly_benefit.yaml`, `monthly_benefit_widow_one_child.yaml` and `monthly_benefit_widow_two_or_more_children.yaml`. Each carries the GR's page, clause and quotes from the change set. No older values were touched.
- **Scheme:** No conditions changed, and no person fields were needed. I added a comment in `schemes/mh/sanjay_gandhi_niradhar.yaml` noting the 2023 revision.
- **Tests:** I added 14 cases to `tests/mh/sanjay_gandhi_niradhar.yaml`. For each widow tier and the general case, there is one case on 4 July 2023 (old amount), one on 5 July 2023 (new amount), and one later in 2026 where applicable. Each cites `GR 202307061137387522 p.1 clause 1`.
- **Changelog:** I added a top entry in English, Hindi and Marathi, linking to the GR.
- **Not changed:** `sources/index.yaml` already registered this GR, so I left it alone.

**Things to check**
- **Quotes not verified against the PDF.** I could not extract text from `sources/mh/202307061137387522.pdf`; the image renderer and the shell both failed, so the quotes are copied from the change set as instructed. Someone should confirm them against the PDF before this is relied on.
- **Widows with 3 or more children.** The change set treats "2 or more" as one tier, so I encoded Rs 1,500 for 3 children too (one test case). This matches the existing structure, where 3 children already get the 2+ amount. It is an interpretation, not an explicit line in the GR's quote.
- **Shell access.** Shell commands needed approval during this run. The test command was approved when I ran it.
